how: Two passes draw each frame. The first renders the world outside the train: real ground along a lake shore, over a river plain and beside a mountain lake, with towns, lamps, stations and rain in the air. The second draws the carriage wall, the window and its glass: beads and runs of water, fog, and the carriage reflected in the pane.

The train stops only now and then. Runs on the glass fall straight down at a stop and stream aft as it gathers speed. The weather eases from one state to the next; with Drift on, it wanders by itself.

notes.title: Moved to the corners bar
notes.text: Weather is a stepper top left with six states; Speed sits bottom right; Time, Drift and Wet glass are in Settings.

notes.title: A shorter line
notes.text: The ride ends across the water from a village with no road, then loops back to the city. It stops at six stations and runs through the rest.

notes.title: A quieter line over the window
notes.text: Only a clock; a stop's name shows as the train pulls in.

notes.title: Shared glass rain
notes.text: Drops on the pane now use the shared shader from Window seat: still beads and thin runs that slant with the train's speed.
